title: Iran-FIFA Zurich Summit Concludes — FIFA Reaffirms Iran's Full Participation; Taj Says FIFA 'Offered Solutions' to All 10 Iranian Demands
detail: The pivotal FIFA-Infantino-Taj summit took place at FIFA headquarters in Zurich on May 20 — described by Yahoo Sports as the meeting that could 'decide Iran's World Cup fate.' The meeting concluded with FIFA reaffirming Iran's participation in all three Group G matches on US soil. Iranian Football Federation President Mehdi Taj confirmed FIFA 'listened to Iran's arguments, the ten points we raised, and that they offered solutions for each one.' FIFA Secretary General Mattias Grafström — who had held preliminary 'excellent and constructive' talks with Taj in Istanbul on May 17 — participated alongside Infantino. While no comprehensive written agreement was publicly released, the outcome was broadly positive: FIFA President Infantino's declaration at the April 30 Vancouver Congress that 'Iran will take part and will play in the United States' remained the operating position. Iran's 10 conditions had included: guaranteed visas for all players and staff without IRGC-related complications, respect for the Iranian flag and national anthem, and security assurances at airports, hotels, and en-route transit routes. Not a single US entry visa had been issued to any Iranian player or coaching staff member as of the close of the Zurich summit — however, Iran's squad members traveled to the US Embassy in Ankara, Turkey the following day to submit visa applications. Iran's Group G schedule remains on US soil: SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles (June 15 vs New Zealand; June 21 vs Belgium) and Lumen Field, Seattle (June 26 vs Egypt). Tournament base camp: Kino Sports Complex, Tucson, Arizona. Warm-up friendly: vs The Gambia in Antalya, May 29. June 1 squad submission deadline: 12 days away. 22 days to kickoff.

media.caption: Iran-FIFA Zurich summit concludes May 20 — FIFA reaffirms Iran's World Cup participation after high-stakes diplomatic meeting

title: Egypt Confirms Mohamed Salah in World Cup Squad — Star Forward Fit Despite Late-Season Hamstring Injury
detail: Egypt announced their preliminary World Cup squad on May 20, with Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah confirmed in the selection despite sustaining a hamstring injury in late April that ended his club season. Egypt's medical staff confirmed Salah is expected to be fit for the tournament — his first match the Group G opener against Belgium on June 15 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. Egypt's Group G is one of the most politically charged at the tournament: they face Iran (June 26 at Lumen Field, Seattle — their only Group G match not in Los Angeles), Belgium, and New Zealand. Salah is the focal point of Egypt's attack; his presence gives the Pharaohs a realistic chance of advancing from a competitive group. Group G is also notable for the Iran visa crisis: the Zurich summit on May 20 took place on the same day Egypt announced their squad, with both teams potentially set to face each other on June 26 in Seattle.

media.caption: Mohamed Salah confirmed in Egypt's World Cup squad for 2026 — Group G opponents include Iran, Belgium, New Zealand
